Anya: Quick sync — customer asked for a single API call that can trigger multiple tool invocations in parallel, then aggregate a structured result. We need a playbook: MVP scope, launch criteria, and how this affects SLOs.
Mike: Do we mean pure fanout (fire all, collect) or a hybrid where some calls must complete in order before others run? The guarantees change everything.
Anya: Mostly fanout with the ability to express soft ordering (e.g., prefer A before B but don't block overall response). Also want per-call timeout and retry policy configurable by client.
Devon: Operational constraints: parallel fanout multiplies backend concurrency. We need a backpressure strategy — per-tenant concurrency cap, queueing limits, and an explicit rejection path. Also require idempotency tokens for retries.
Sara: From ML side, if we do parallel tool calling with model-driven prompts we have to preserve KV cache semantics if second calls reuse context from first. So either disallow direct KV sharing across parallel branches or add explicit merge semantics.
Kevin: UX ask: client needs a predictable final schema. Recommend we expose a light DSL for aggregation: e.g., {"branches": [{"call":"extract_entities","optional":true}], "merge_strategy":"first_success|collect_all"}. Keep it small for MVP.
Mike: Implementation notes: backend will map each branch to a route; we can reuse existing tool invocation infra but must add a coordinator that enforces global budgets and cancels inflight branches when global timeout is hit. Cancellation must be best-effort.
Devon: For retries: prefer client-controlled retry hints. Server will do at-most-once unless client supplies idempotency key. We'll also surface retry-budget headers: `X-RI-Retry-Budget: 3` and `X-RI-Request-Id`.
Anya: Launch criteria proposal: 1) API shape stable (DSL v0), 2) docs + examples for common patterns, 3) e2e latency budget defined (p50, p90 targets for small fanout), 4) canary with 1-2 trusted customers, 5) observability: per-branch latency + failure breakdown.
Sara: Quality gating: include prompt-level replay tests (fixed seeds) to ensure aggregation semantics don't regress. Also add smoke checks for merge_strategy behaviors.
Kevin: UX constraint — default must be conservative: `merge_strategy=first_success` and `max_branches=5` to avoid surprising costs. Clients opt into larger budgets.
Mike: MVP scope suggestion: support fanout with `collect_all` and `first_success`, per-branch timeout, per-request global timeout, basic retry hints, and structured JSON merge. Leave dependent-sequencing and KV-shared branches for v2.
Anya: Sounds good. Action items: Mike + Sara to draft API proto and example payloads by EOD Friday; Devon to propose quota/backpressure limits and cancellation semantics; Kevin to produce two UX examples for docs; I'll line up two customers for canary. :thumbsup:
orchestrator-bot: Checklist created: [API draft], [Quota proposal], [Docs UX], [Canary run].
Devon: One more: add clear error model for partial failures (HTTP 207-like) and a clear contract for idempotency and retries.
Anya: Agreed — include a `partial_result` field and explicit error codes. We'll reconvene Monday after drafts.
